_comment:
Slow. Everything else in the joy set is quick, and this one is the opposite - a small sink, then a long eased swell, then a HOLD of nearly a second where nothing moves at all, then the settle. The hold is the joke: pride is funny in proportion to how long the character stays inflated with nobody applauding.

The smooth part is a whole-actor `scaleBy` (which TWEENS); the chest-out is an ad-hoc `parts` transform on body + head (which SNAPS) landing at the TOP of the swell, so the puff arrives as one frame after a slow rise. That contrast is the entire effect and it costs no art.

`scaleBy` NOT `scale` - staging places characters at 0.62, so an absolute 1.12 would be a giant. The gag returns to scaleBy 1.0 and parts {} so it leaves nothing behind for the rest of the scene.

Deliberately NOT animated: arms on hips, a strut, any clip. There is no arm part to trust.
triggers: drew himself up to his full height
draws himself up to his full height

agent._comment: body and head are both guaranteed by ToonRigRepair; needsAnyOf is ANY-of, so one entry is enough to declare the tier.

beats._comment: taken aback first - the compliment landing. Swelling straight from happy has no arc.
the sink. 3% down, and it is anticipation - the audience has to see him get smaller before he gets bigger.
the swell itself, deliberately slow - 0.75s of eased travel. The tiny dy lifts him onto his toes as he inflates. RELATIVE to whatever mark he stands on.
the face turns during the rise, not at the top - so the change is already made when the chest pops
chest out, chin up, arriving on ONE frame at the top of the eased swell. Parts snap; that is why this reads as a puff and not as more of the same tween.
the only thing that happens during the hold. Nearly a second where the character does not move is the point - do not fill it.
the deflate, snapping back to rest in one frame while the body scale is still up. Empty transform set = rig's own rest pose.
tidy up. scaleBy back to 1.0 and dy back to the mark - position and scale carry to the end of the SCENE, so a gag that does not restore them is permanent.
